review.summary: Static review of the supplied text only; no tests were run and none are claimed. No BLOCKER or MAJOR defects found. Both callers clear the error text while pending, so the pending true->false transition re-triggers focus and the alert re-announces on repeated identical errors. Remaining items are minor robustness, test-coverage and polish concerns: unconditional focus stealing, effect/retry paths untested by static-markup tests, duplicated success text in the funnel renderer, and possible layout gaps from always-mounted empty regions.

findings.issue: Error focus is moved unconditionally to the alert paragraph whenever an error appears and pending is false, regardless of where focus currently is.
findings.evidence: `useEffect(() => { if (errorMessage && !pending) errorRef.current?.focus(); }, [errorMessage, pending]);` has no check of document.activeElement. In lead-form the inputs are not shown as disabled while status === "loading" (only the button is), so a user can move to or edit another field while the request is pending.
findings.impact: A late failure can pull keyboard/screen-reader focus away from a field the user is actively editing, which is disruptive. Recovery is only needed when focus was lost (body) or was on the submit control that became disabled.
findings.recommended_fix: Capture whether focus was on the submit control/within the form (or on body) when pending began, and only call focus() when document.activeElement is body/null, the submit button, or the feedback region itself. Optionally pass focusOnError={false} for callers that manage focus themselves.
findings.required_test: DOM test (jsdom/RTL): focus an input, toggle pending true->false with an error, assert focus stays on the input; with focus on body or the disabled submit button, assert focus lands on the alert element.

findings.area: whole file (all four tests use renderToStaticMarkup)
findings.issue: The focus-recovery and repeated-retry behaviors named in the task are not exercised; static markup rendering never runs useEffect.
findings.evidence: All tests call `renderToStaticMarkup`, which does not execute effects or re-render, so `errorRef.current?.focus()` and the pending false->true->false sequence are never validated. Only initial markup strings are asserted.
findings.impact: A regression that removes or breaks focus restoration, or that stops re-focusing on a second identical error, would pass the suite.
findings.recommended_fix: Add client-render tests that mount the component, rerender through error -> pending -> same error, and assert document.activeElement and region text at each step.
findings.required_test: RTL test: render error (expect focus on role=alert); rerender pending (alert empty, status shows progress, no focus change); rerender with identical error (expect focus restored again and alert text re-populated); render with no error on mount (expect no focus).

findings.issue: Success message is rendered twice: once via the sr-only polite status region and again as a visible plain paragraph with no role.
findings.evidence:
`successMessage={status === "success" ? message : ""}` is passed to the feedback component, and `{status === "success" && message ?

{message}

: null}` renders the same text visibly.
findings.impact: Screen-reader users in browse mode hear the success text twice (sr-only span plus visible paragraph). The live announcement is intended, but the duplicate content is redundant.
findings.recommended_fix: Either mark the visible paragraph aria-hidden (keeping the status region as the announcement), or let the shared component render the visible success text itself in a single polite region (visible, not sr-only) and drop the extra paragraph.
findings.required_test: Render funnel form in success state and assert the message appears exactly once in the accessibility tree (or that the visible copy is aria-hidden).

findings.issue: Refocus/re-announce for a repeated identical error depends on the caller toggling pending or changing the message; there is no explicit retry token.
findings.evidence: Effect deps are only `errorMessage` and `pending`. Both supplied callers blank the message while pending, so network retries work, but a caller that sets the same error again without a pending transition (e.g. a client-side validation or verification-not-ready path that sets status "error" directly) produces no dep change, no focus move, and no live-region text change.
findings.impact: Repeated identical failures from non-pending paths could be silent for keyboard/screen-reader users. Not demonstrable from the supplied text because those handler paths are not shown.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept an optional `errorKey`/attempt counter prop (incremented per failed attempt) included in the effect deps and used to remount or re-write the alert text; document that callers must either toggle pending or supply the key.
findings.required_test: Rerender twice with the same errorMessage, pending=false, and an incremented errorKey; assert focus is restored after the user moves focus away and the alert text is re-announced.

findings.issue: Always-mounted empty alert paragraph is a real layout child, and the focused alert element may be double-announced by some screen readers.
findings.evidence:
The `

` is rendered even when empty. In callers using grid gap or space-y spacing (lead-form previously rendered nothing there), an empty child can still add an inter-item gap. The same element is both role="alert" (aria-live assertive) and programmatically focused with tabIndex -1.
findings.impact: Possible extra blank spacing above the submit button before any error, and potential duplicate announcement (live-region change plus focus announcement) in some AT combinations. Both are cosmetic/minor; layout classes are not in the supplied scope.
findings.recommended_fix: Use `empty:hidden`/`min-h-0 m-0` or hidden-when-empty styling that keeps the node mounted, and verify in a screen reader that focus plus role=alert does not double-announce; if it does, keep role=alert but only focus when text is present and consider role="alert" without aria-live duplication.
findings.required_test: Visual check of both forms before/after change for unchanged spacing; manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass confirming a single announcement of the error.
